Modern.brandNameRationale: Two words from the vinyl tradition. Side A is the lead-off side of the record, the songs the artist wanted heard first. The label is named after the strongest material, not the catalog. Plain, modern, and immediately legible to anyone who has held a record.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern independent record labels are competing with major labels on artist development and with streaming platforms on direct relationships. The successful labels look like product companies with editorial taste, releasing fewer artists more carefully.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Sub Pop (subpop.com) holds the heritage indie label position. XL Recordings (xlrecordings.com) sits in the modern indie tier. 4AD (4ad.com) is the design-led peer. Ninja Tune (ninjatune.net) holds the electronic-leaning middle. We sit closest to 4AD in posture.
Modern.positioningStatement: An independent label that releases the album the artist would have made anyway.

targetAudience.primary: Musicians at the small-label stage of their career. Listeners who follow labels as much as artists. Reads Pitchfork and Loud and Quiet weekly.

dos: Speak to the listener and the musician at once

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark only. SIDE A in a tight modern grotesk, all caps, two words on one line with a small period after A. A standalone A-with-period mark used as the catalog sticker on every record sleeve.

colorPalette.name: Label White
colorPalette.meaning: Old paper label. Used as space.

colorPalette.name: Signal Orange
colorPalette.meaning: Inner sleeve color. The single accent.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and album titles
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for credits and track listings
typography.rationale: One family. The mono carries the track times, credits, and catalog numbers. The regular carries the brand and the album titles.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No major-label distribution deals. No Spotify-playlist gaming. No 'sync' as the primary revenue strategy. No artist-development contracts that lock the artist for ten years.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: Physical records (vinyl, cassette) shipped with a printed insert. Digital downloads delivered with the same insert as a PDF. A bi-monthly printed catalog mailed to subscribers. A small year-end party in the label's city.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Two words. Atrium is the older architectural word for the central open space of a great house. Records names the category cleanly. The pair reads as a heritage label with a small catalog of important recordings, the way a great library has a small collection of important books.
Luxury.story: Atrium Records began with three principals who had spent decades inside major labels and large publishers, and wanted to release a small number of recordings with the kind of care those institutions could not give. The label releases between four and eight albums a year. The catalog is small on purpose.
Luxury.industrySummary: Top end recorded music has been moving toward catalog acquisition and licensing portfolios. There's a parallel market for small labels that release new recordings with archival care. The customer is paying for the recording, the pressing, the booklet, and the long relationship with the label.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: ECM Records (ecmrecords.com) is the peer in jazz and contemporary classical. Erased Tapes (erasedtapes.com) holds the design-led modern classical position. Domino Recording (dominorecordco.com) sits in the indie heritage tier. We sit closest to ECM in posture.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A label that releases recordings as if they were books.

targetAudience.primary: Adults who buy music on physical formats. Subscribers to The Wire, Loud and Quiet, or Wax Poetics. Listeners who collect a label more than they collect an artist. Often work in design, architecture, or other adjacent disciplines.

dos: Write release notes like editorial essays
Speak in the language of the music
donts: Promote releases on social media with reels
Sign deals based on streaming projections

Luxury.logoDirection: A classical serif wordmark with elegant ligatures. A small hand-drawn archway-shaped hallmark, used on the spine of every record sleeve, the catalog booklet, and the wax seal of every paper letter.

colorPalette.name: Library Green
colorPalette.meaning: Bookbinding leather, the spine of an old volume.

typography.primary: Canela Text for the wordmark and album titles
typography.secondary: Söhne for the catalog booklets and digital
typography.rationale: A high contrast classical serif sets the heritage tone. A modern grotesk handles the credits and the digital surfaces.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No catalog acquisition strategy. No sync-licensing as primary revenue. No social media manager. No streaming-playlist relationships.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Single word. Record is the most basic word for the medium. It works as a noun (the physical object) and a verb (the act of making music). The brand puts the medium in the brand position, plain and direct.
Minimal.industrySummary: Most music brands compete on artist signing, catalog scale, and streaming presence. There's an opening for a label that releases only physical records and ignores the rest.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most labels operate digital-first. Sacred Bones (sacredbonesrecords.com), Mexican Summer (mexicansummer.com), and Dead Oceans (deadoceans.com) all do physical, but with broader catalogs. The closest spirit is some early Touch & Go: tight, physical, opinionated.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A label that releases only on vinyl, with no streaming presence.

targetAudience.primary: Music collectors who already own a turntable. They want to buy the record, hold it, and play it. They don't need a Spotify link.

dos: Confirm orders with one short message

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. RECORD in a single weight grotesk, wide kerned, all caps. No icon. The label on the center of every record is the wordmark, the catalog number, and the side indicator. That's the whole identity system.

typography.rationale: One face. The record label, the sleeve, and the receipt all carry the same wordmark.

customSections.title: Not this
customSections.body: No streaming releases. No social media. No newsletter. No tour announcements. No artist photos in the catalog.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Three words. Aria is the operatic word for a featured vocal piece, suggesting heritage and seriousness. Music Group names the holding-company category. The whole name reads like a real, established music-industry holding company, the kind that already shows up on the deck of every investment bank covering the sector.
Corporate.industrySummary: Music rights and catalog services is a multi-billion-dollar B2B category. Catalog acquisitions, music publishing, sync licensing, and royalty administration are dominated by major labels and a few large independent publishers. The opening is a structured mid-size firm focused on the contemporary catalog tier.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Hipgnosis Songs Fund (hipgnosissongs.com) holds the catalog-investment peer position. Concord Music (concord.com) is the independent holding company at scale. BMG (bmg.com) sits in the same tier. Primary Wave (primarywave.com) does artist-services-led acquisition. We sit smaller, focused on the contemporary indie catalog.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A music rights holding company building a portfolio of contemporary catalogs and artist services.
Corporate.positioningRationale: Independent labels, songwriter estates, and artist catalogs need scale partners that won't bury them inside a major. We sit between the majors and the boutique advisors, with the operational discipline a serious investor needs.

targetAudience.primary: Music industry executives, label founders considering acquisition, songwriter estate representatives, and institutional investors evaluating music rights as an asset class.
motivations: Long-term capital commitment to the catalogs
Sync and licensing infrastructure without majors-style oversight

dos: Speak to the investor and the catalog owner

messagingPillars.name: Portfolio approach
messagingPillars.description: Multiple catalogs and artist services lines under one operating group, each maintaining its own identity.

messagingPillars.name: Long-term capital
messagingPillars.description: Catalogs held for decades. Founders and estate representatives retain creative and editorial authority over the catalogs they sell to us.

messagingPillars.name: Operational depth
messagingPillars.description: Royalty administration, sync, publishing, and rights enforcement under one organization, with technology investments that the majors are slow to make.

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark to the left. The mark is a single fermata symbol reduced to two strokes, suggesting held music. Reads cleanly on a quarterly investor deck, a contract folder, and a B2B trade show booth.

colorPalette.name: Brass
colorPalette.meaning: Music industry accent, the brass of a horn.

typography.primary: Inter for marketing and B2B materials
typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed annual reports
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean across digital. The serif handles formal annual reports and printed investor materials.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No direct-to-consumer streaming. No retail records under the parent brand. No artist-roster marketing on social media. The holding company is not a brand for listeners.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Two words. B Side is the second side of a record, traditionally the experimental or underrated track. The label is named after the cult position: the work that doesn't get played on the radio but stays with the listener longer. Loud, slightly cheeky, and on the customer's tongue already.
Creative.manifesto: Most labels release the single, push the single, and hope the single carries the album. We made B Side because the songs that change people are usually the ones the artist almost cut. We sign the artist for the B sides. We promote the B sides. We are not a hit factory. We are a B side factory.
Creative.industrySummary: Music label branding has been polished and risk-averse. There's room for a label that's loud, opinionated, sticker-friendly, and still releases music that holds up in twenty years.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Stones Throw (stonesthrowrecords.com) holds the cult-indie position. Numero Group (numerogroup.com) does the reissue-led version. Awesome Tapes from Africa (awesometapes.com) sits in the discovery tier. We are sharper and louder than any of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: An indie label for artists whose B sides outlast their singles.

targetAudience.primary: 20s and 30s. Already follows three indie labels. Buys records on Bandcamp. Wears the merch. Tells friends about the B sides specifically.

dos: Make jokes about the music industry
donts: Sand the edges off the music in marketing

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a punchy display serif with the B set in a slightly thicker stroke, suggesting the cult side of the record. Standalone B icon for stickers, social profiles, and the back of every record sleeve.

colorPalette.name: B Side Red
colorPalette.usage: Primary brand color, hero surfaces, stickers

typography.primary: Migra for the wordmark and big display
typography.secondary: PP Neue Montreal for body and credits
typography.rationale: Migra has personality. Neue Montreal handles the credits. The pair feels designed and a little defiant.

customSections.title: What it isn't
customSections.body: Not a streaming-first label. Not a chart label. Not afraid of red. Not too cool to make a joke about itself.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: Records shipped with a sticker, a printed insert, and a hand-numbered card. A small in-person showcase the first Friday of every month. A monthly newsletter with the artists' actual emails included. Hoodies that say B SIDE in across the back.
